title.narrative: CO Rio Bogota Environmental Recuperation and Flood Control Project

description.narrative: The objective of the Project is to assist the Borrower to transform the Rio Bogota river into an environmental asset for the BogotaDistrito Capital metropolitan region by improving water quality, reducing flood risks, and creating multi-functional areas along the river.

The objective of the Rio Bogota Environmental Recuperation and Flood Control Project for Colombia is to assist the Borrower to transform the Rio Bogota River into an environmental asset for the Bogota Distrito Capital metropolitan region by improving water quality, reducing flood risks and creating multi-functional areas along the river. There are four components to the project, the first component being upgrading and expansion of the Salitre Wastewater Treatment Plant (WWTP). The second component is the flood control and Rio Bogota environmental restoration works. This component will reduce flood risk and establishment of multifunctional zones along the Rio Bogota river through the carrying out of flood control and environmental improvement works, including river dredging, embankment construction, restoration of riparian habitats, meanders and wetlands, land acquisition, involuntary displacement of people, landscape design, and establishment of parks, and the provision of consultants' services for the design, construction and supervision therefor. The third component is the environmental and water studies. Finally, the fourth component is the project management and administration. This component will strengthening the capacity of the Borrower for the day-to-day implementation of the project, including: (a) compliance with financial, environmental and procurement management, reporting requirements and monitoring and supervision activities, implementation of the Resettlement Action Plan (RAP) and Environmental Management Plan (EMP), (b) the carrying out of a public outreach campaign, (c) training, and (d) the provision of consultants' services therefor.

title.narrative: People under reduced risk of flooding as a result of the Project

comment.narrative: <p>Target achieved and surpassed. The difference between the set target value and the achieved final value results from differences between the population growth assumptions used at the time of Project appraisal (calculating that Bogotá would have 7 million people by 2020) and the actual population to date (approximately 7.8 million as estimated by the National Department of Statistics [DANE] based on the most recent census [2018]).</p>

comment.narrative: <p>Target achieved. The EAAB financed a Biosolids Management Plan consultancy, which assessed different types of biosolids and viable alternatives, along with considerations for implementing the latter in the short, medium, and long terms, and proposals for potential necessary regulatory adjustments to accommodate them.</p>

title.narrative: Study for the Design of Multifunctional Areas and the Operation and Maintenance Plan for the flood control works under component 2 completed.
The Salitre WWTP meets effluent discharge limits for BOD, TSS and total coliform

comment.narrative:
<p>The BOD and TSS limits are met as of project closing. Conditions to achieve the coliform target are in place but target is currently not being pursued due to changed discharge requirements achieved. </p>
<p>The plant has installed and tested the necessary equipment to conduct the chlorination process that would allow the effluent to meet the total coliforms target. However, since theoriginally planned diversion of treated wastewater has not been formally agreed to with the La Ramada agriculture district members given the additional costs this would imply for them, the decision was made to not undertake the chlorination process until such agreement is reached. In the meantime, the non-implementation of this process allows for reduced operational costs while still complying with the national regulatory requirements for water quality of WWTP effluents discharged directly into rivers as mandated by the Ministry of Environment and Sustainable Development in Resolution 631 of 2015.</p>
